claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent more than a hundred thousand years getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: Mitalas & Sills 1992, ApJ 401, 759-760 (NASA ADS scan, both pages read; Crossref confirms doi:10.1086/172103); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched 2026-11-17); NASA SVS 11084 (fetched with the verified CA bundle); Crossref record for Stix 2003 (doi:10.1023/A:1022952621810)
claims.note: MS92 abstract: 0.090 cm average step 'gives 1.7 x 10^5 yr for the diffision time scale of the present Sun'; section 3: t_d = 1.7 x 10^5 yr is the time for a diffusing photon to reach the inner edge of the convective zone, and convective crossing only adds time. MSFC: 'This energy diffuses outward by radiation' and a photon 'takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Both exceed 1e5 yr, so 'more than a hundred thousand years' is a true lower bound (1.7e5 is within A3's rounding limit). SVS's '40,000 years' disagrees; the disagreement is recorded in SOURCES and the peer-reviewed figure is preferred, which A3 allows, but see claim 19 for a misstatement in that record. Stix 2003: only bibliographic data (Solar Physics 212, 3-6, 2003) confirmed on Crossref; the 3e7 yr figure was not read at source, and the hook does not rest on it.

claims.claim: Hook alone (viewer swipes at second two): the energy reaching you as sunlight took over 100,000 years to escape the Sun.
claims.source_checked: Same as claim 1 (Mitalas & Sills 1992; NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior')
claims.note: The first sentence is about the energy, not a single photon, and claims only a lower bound, so it does not carry the popular 'the photon hitting you is 100,000 years old' error. Nothing false is left if the viewer leaves after it (A4).

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: NIST CODATA 2022 c (physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?c): 299 792 458 m/s exact; NASA SVS 11084: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel the 93 million miles from the sun to Earth'; IAU 2012 Resolution B2 PDF could NOT be read (iau.org returned 404 / an HTML page); cross-check only: NSSDC Earth fact sheet (semimajor axis 149.598e6 km, perihelion 147.095e6, aphelion 152.100e6 km)
claims.note: 1 AU / c = 499.0 s = 8 min 19 s; the NSSDC perihelion/aphelion give 8.18-8.46 min, matching SOURCES' 8.2-8.5 min and +/-1.7%. 'Eight minutes' is stated outright by NASA SVS, which SOURCES cites (claim 5). The IAU value itself was not read at source; this does not affect the verdict because SVS and CODATA carry the line. Optional: add the NSSDC Earth fact sheet to SOURCES 1 as a reachable agency figure for the distance.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.source_checked: Follows from claims 1 and 3 (Mitalas & Sills 1992; NASA MSFC; NASA SVS; CODATA c)
claims.note: More than 1e5 years against about 8 minutes. No new number.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.note: Read with the next sentence it means not the same kind of light. MSFC: the energy diffuses by radiation 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays' and 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. It does not claim the photons are different particles (SOURCES 4 correctly records that no reachable source says that).

claims.claim: It starts as gamma rays and leaves as sunlight.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (pp-chain paragraph and radiative-zone paragraph)
claims.note: 'Leaves as sunlight' is supported ('leaves the surface as visible light'). 'Starts as gamma rays' overstates the source. MSFC says the pp chain's second step makes 'a helium-3 nucleus and a gamma ray' (step 1 makes a positron and neutrino; step 3 releases two protons, so not all the energy starts as gamma rays) and that the radiation carrying the energy is 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays'. At the core's 15 MK the thermal radiation peaks in X-rays, so a pedant will object. Change to the source's wording, e.g. 'Inside, it travels as gamma rays and X-rays. It leaves as sunlight.' (or 'It starts as gamma rays and X-rays and leaves as sunlight.'), and update SOURCES 4 to quote the line as changed.

claims.source_checked: Rests on claim 1 (Mitalas & Sills 1992; NASA MSFC)
claims.note: More than 1e5 years in transit fits 'ancient' as plain English. No new number.

claims.claim: Its last eight minutes were the trip to you.
claims.note: SVS: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel ... from the sun to Earth.'

claims.claim: Tag '8 MINUTES' / sub 'surface to your skin' + 'not to scale', over the Sun-Earth shot with a bright pulse crossing the gap
claims.where: on-screen: 8 MINUTES tag over Sun-Earth shot
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084; CODATA c; NSSDC Earth fact sheet (cross-check)
claims.note: 8 min 19 s from the photosphere rounds to 8 minutes, and SVS states 'eight minutes'. The pulse is schematic and the shot says 'not to scale' (A6); SOURCES 6 notes Earth is drawn too big and too close.

claims.claim: Tag '100,000+ YEARS' / sub 'energy, core to surface' + 'not to scale'
claims.source_checked: Mitalas & Sills 1992; NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'
claims.note: MS92's 1.7e5 yr runs from the centre to the base of the convection zone and MSFC gives about 1e6 yr to the interface layer; the convective crossing only adds time, so core to surface is more than 100,000 years. It says 'energy', not 'photon', which matches MSFC's 'This energy diffuses outward'.

claims.claim: Tag 'THE ENERGY' / sub '100,000+ years getting out'
claims.source_checked: Mitalas & Sills 1992; NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'

claims.claim: Tag 'THE TRIP' / sub '8 minutes to you' + 'not to scale' (Sun-Earth shot)
claims.where: on-screen: THE TRIP tag over Sun-Earth shot
claims.note: Same basis as claim 3; the not-to-scale label is shown.

claims.claim: Sun cutaway with rings at 0.25 R (core edge) and 0.7 R (base of convection zone)
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; Crossref record for Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson 1991 (ApJ 378, 413, doi:10.1086/170441), bibliographic data only
claims.note: MSFC: core is 'the innermost 25%', the radiative zone runs 'from 25% ... to 70%', and the convection zone is 'the outermost 30%'. The 0.713 R helioseismic value (CDG91) was not read at source, but the animation uses MSFC's 0.7 and does not depend on it.

claims.claim: Random-walk path drawn from the centre out to the 0.7 ring, with short side-stubs
claims.source_checked: Mitalas & Sills 1992 (sections 2-3); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'
claims.note: MS92 models a random walk from the centre to the inner edge of the convective zone; MSFC describes photons that 'bounce from particle to particle through the radiative zone'. Schematic, and the shot carries 'not to scale' (a 0.09 cm step cannot be drawn).

claims.claim: Path colour runs violet toward pale yellow by log temperature: 15 MK at r=0, 7 MK at 0.25 R, 2 MK at 0.7 R, 5,700 K at the surface (about 10% of the way to yellow at 0.25 R, 26% at 0.7 R)
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; arithmetic recomputed
claims.note: MSFC gives the centre at 'about 15,000,000 C', the radiative zone falling 'from 7,000,000 C to about 2,000,000 C', and the surface at 5,700 K. Log fractions: (log 15e6 - log 7e6)/(log 15e6 - log 5700) = 0.097 (~10%), and for 2e6 = 0.256 (~26%), as stated. The hue is schematic and only signals that the radiation softens as the temperature drops; the path stays far from yellow (X-ray, not visible) at 0.7 R.

claims.claim: Rotating dashed circles (convection cells) fill the shell between 0.7 R and the surface
claims.note: MSFC: energy crosses the outermost 30% by 'convective fluid flows (boiling motion)', and 'These convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface'.

claims.claim: A fan of five short yellow light rays leaves the surface
claims.note: MSFC: the energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. The ray count is decorative.

claims.claim: SOURCES coverage (A1/A2): every spoken and on-screen claim has a numbered entry citing an A2 source
claims.source_checked: script/age-of-sunlight.txt SOURCES entries 1-6, checked against the sources opened above
claims.note: Each line has an entry: 1 (IAU, CODATA; SVS in 5), 2 (MS92 peer-reviewed, MSFC agency), 3 (derived), 4 (MSFC, SVS), 5 (SVS), 6 (MSFC, CDG91) for the animation and the not-to-scale labels. Quotes from MS92, MSFC and SVS match their sources word for word, including MS92's 'diffision' typo. Stix is marked 'not re-read at source', as A2 requires.

claims.claim: SOURCES 2 disagreement record: 'SVS's 40,000 sits at the top of that superseded range' (MS92's 3 x 10^3 to 3 x 10^4 yr)
claims.source_checked: Mitalas & Sills 1992, section 1 (ADS scan); NASA SVS 11084
claims.note: MS92's range for the common 0.5-1.0 cm step is 3 x 10^3 to 3 x 10^4 yr. SVS's 40,000 (4 x 10^4) is above that range, not 'at the top' of it, and SVS gives no method, so MS92 does not explain the 40,000 'directly'. Also, SVS times the photon to 'the sun's surface', not to 0.7 R. Reword, e.g.: 'SVS gives no method or step length. Its 40,000 is just above the 3e3-3e4 yr that MS92 says the common 0.5-1.0 cm step gives ("much too short") and about four times below MS92's 1.7e5, so the script follows the peer-reviewed figure and MSFC's ~1e6.' The spoken hook can stay as it is; this fix is to the A3 record only.
